    Biography

    I am Victoria Knapp Perez, a Ph.D. candidate in Physics at the University of California, Irvine (UCI), specializing in machine learning for scientific discovery and AI-driven model design. My work bridges reinforcement learning, deep learning, and computational physics, focusing on how intelligent systems can autonomously construct and validate scientific models.

    Before joining UCI, I earned my B.Sc. in Physics from the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), graduating cum laude. My academic foundation in theoretical physics and my professional experience in AI research position me at the intersection of automated reasoning, symbolic-numerical modeling, and scientific machine learning.

    AI Research Overview

    My research focuses on developing AI frameworks that can automate reasoning and model discovery in complex physical systems. I co-developed the Autonomous Model Builder (AMBer), a reinforcement learning framework that autonomously constructs and evaluates theoretical particle physics models. AMBer integrates OpenAI Gym–style environments, Stable-Baselines PPO agents, and high-performance computing (HPC) to explore symmetry groups, optimize model parameters, and improve predictive accuracy with minimal human intervention. This represents one of the first AI-assisted approaches to symbolic scientific model generation.

    Beyond physics, I am broadly interested in how learning algorithms can replicate and extend human scientific reasoning. I have experience in fine-tuning large language models (LLMs), developing deep learning pipelines (PyTorch, FastAI, Hugging Face), and optimizing distributed training workflows on HPC systems.

    Software Development

    I am one of the creators and maintainers of FlavorBuilder, a Python toolkit for symbolic model construction and data-driven analysis in particle physics. Built for extensibility and performance, FlavorBuilder provides APIs for generating mass matrices, computing observables, and fitting theoretical models to experimental data. The package is available open-source on GitHub and PyPI. Part of this software is partly the translation of Discrete. Detailed documentation and citation guidelines are provided in the GitHub repository.
